definitions.explanation: The rise and fall of the voice when speaking, which affects meaning, emotion, and naturalness of speech.

examples.japanese: イントネーション⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}をつけて⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: To speak paying attention to intonation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{関西弁|かんさいべん}→関西弁：17855_kansaiben⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{標準語|ひょうじゅんご}→標準語：07421_hyoujungo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧イントネーション⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Kansai dialect and standard Japanese have different intonation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{単語|たんご}→単語：03413_tango⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧イントネーション⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧⟦{発音|はつおん}→発音：01698_hatsuon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{身|み}につける→身につける：03158_minitsukeru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: In Japanese, changing the intonation of a word can change its meaning, so learning correct pronunciation is important.

notes:
From English "intonation." In Japanese linguistics, intonation is particularly important because Japanese is a pitch-accent language. The pitch pattern of a word can distinguish meaning — for example, ⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧ (bridge) and ⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧ (chopsticks) differ only in pitch accent. Regional dialects are also distinguished largely by their intonation patterns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- イントネーション⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧: the intonation is different
- イントネーション⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{気|き}をつける→気をつける：09771_kiwotsukeru⟧: to pay attention to intonation
- ⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧イントネーション: correct intonation
- イントネーション⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧: intonation practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦アクセント→アクセント：10697_akusento⟧: accent — in Japanese linguistics, often refers to pitch accent on individual words, while イントネーション refers to the melody of phrases and sentences
- ⟦{抑揚|よくよう}→抑揚：12780_yokuyou⟧: intonation; inflection — the native Japanese equivalent, used in more formal or literary contexts
- {声調|せいちょう}: tone — used specifically for tonal languages like Chinese
